notes: seconds: wall time of the whole process (start-up included); inner_seconds: the calculation inside it (tblite, axtb Python: without interpreter start-up and imports; axtb CLI: its own 'seconds'; axtb Hessians: the Hessian alone)
max_rss_mb is not the program's peak memory: Linux carries the (v)forked driver's high-water RSS into the child at exec, so it is max(driver's peak so far, program's peak) and mostly the driver's
other_busy_threads: average busy hardware threads of the machine during the run (/proc/stat) minus the run's own CPU use; the laptop has 16 hardware threads on 8 cores
note_session: the first energy + gradient session (2026-11-07 07:04-07:27 UTC) and the Hessians; session2/ holds a second, independent energy + gradient session (10:22-10:45 UTC). In both the desktop file indexer kept about one hardware thread busy (other_busy_threads median 1.1)
